summary: Inspect raw texture roles, packed channels, color-space meaning and full material response separately under a controlled lighting and display setup.
objective: A material mismatch identifies the texture role, channel, UV set, factor, transfer function and runtime binding responsible instead of being hidden by a beauty render.
applies_when: A metallic-roughness material looks too glossy, flat, dark, tinted or incorrectly occluded after export.
intent_signals: base color looks too dark after export
normal map changes when color management changes
example_prompts: Add a diagnostic mode that shows each glTF material role and packed ORM channel.
Trace a glossy runtime material back to its roughness texture, factor and UV set.
negative_signals: display every data map as sRGB color
not_for: Choosing an artistic material without a parity question.

principles: Separate raw-data inspection from shaded-response inspection. A grayscale channel view confirms stored values and binding; a neutral PBR fixture confirms how factors, lights and view direction use them.
Inspect one material and one role at a time while keeping geometry, UV selection, environment, direct lights, exposure, tone mapping and output transform recorded.
Treat base color and emissive RGB as encoded color inputs, and metallic, roughness, occlusion and normal data as non-color roles under the glTF contract.
A packed texture file is not one semantic image: report the channel assigned to each role and ignore unused channels only when the target material contract does.
implementation: Inventory the source material, exported glTF material and loaded runtime material by stable node/material IDs. Record texture URI or embedded image identity, role, channel, coordinate set, transform, sampler, scalar factor and color-space annotation.

Provide disposable raw views for base-color RGB/alpha, metallic blue, roughness green, occlusion red, normal RGB and emissive RGB. Label whether values are shown encoded or decoded; do not run data maps through a color interpretation silently.

Provide a separate neutral shaded fixture with fixed camera, diffuse/specular light directions, environment, exposure and display transform. Toggle one role or factor at a time through cloned diagnostics while production material remains unchanged.

Check ORM channel packing against the material bindings, then inspect normal orientation and occlusion behavior separately. Use the linked handoff records for Blender node-to-glTF translation and tangent basis.
Reset restores original materials and shared textures, removes clones and returns lighting, exposure and tone mapping to the captured baseline.
observable_checks: Use a synthetic texture with distinct red, green and blue ramps; raw views and bindings identify occlusion, roughness and metalness without relying on the final shaded appearance.
Toggle base color, roughness, metallic, normal, occlusion and emissive roles one at a time under a fixed fixture; only the declared material response changes.

Switch a color input between correct and deliberately wrong transfer annotation while leaving data maps unchanged; the report names the role and annotation rather than calling the whole material dark.
Exit inspection and compare material IDs, texture references, factors, environment, exposure and display transform with the captured baseline.

creative_affordances: Use a channel grid, wipe comparison or selected-pixel readout according to the failure.
Pair raw maps with a neutral sphere or the actual object, clearly labeling which view answers which question.
known_limits: A channel inspection does not prove artistic match or identical pixels across Blender and Three.js.
Extensions and custom shaders may add roles beyond core metallic-roughness and require their own declared diagnostics.
Authored source-checked diagnostic guidance; no material export, upload or render was run.

claims.statement: Core glTF metallic-roughness materials encode base-color texture RGB with the sRGB transfer function, pack roughness in the green and metalness in the blue channel of a linear metallicRoughnessTexture, use the red channel of an occlusion texture for indirect-light occlusion, and define tangent-space normal textures with linear RGB component mapping.
claims.scope: Core glTF 2.0 texture roles; material factors, UV binding, renderer lighting and extensions must also be inspected.
